column1: SECTION F — TEACHER'S SUBJECT KNOWLEDGE   |   Assessed through lesson observation. Does the teacher demonstrate accurate, deep understanding of the content?

column3: Teacher makes factual errors that go uncorrected.
column4: Mostly accurate but with minor errors or imprecise language.
column5: Content is accurate; no errors observed.
column6: Content is accurate AND teacher explains WHY (conceptual depth, not just facts).
column8:
FICO V3 (B9) + TEACH (Lesson Facilitation) + HOTS Observation Form (Practice #2: 'Teacher's explanation of content is clear and correct')

Why: 15–25% of teachers in LMICs make content errors. If the teacher doesn't know the content, nothing else matters.

column3: Incorrect or no subject-specific terminology used.
column4: Some terms used but not explained or used inconsistently.
column5: Key terms used accurately and explained to students.
column6: Terms used naturally; students also use them; bilingual bridging (Urdu/English) effective.
column8:
FICO V3 (B10) + OECD (Instructional Clarity) + Training Curriculum (Content Expertise: vocabulary, grammar, academic language)

Why: Academic language is the medium of assessment. Students who don't learn the vocabulary can't pass the exam.

column3: Teacher unaware of common misconceptions in this topic.
column4: Aware but doesn't address them proactively.
column5: Anticipates and addresses at least 1–2 common misconceptions.
column6: Systematically surfaces and corrects misconceptions; uses diagnostic questions.
column8:
FICO V3 (B11) + TEACH (Checks for Understanding) + Training Curriculum L1 (diagnosing misconceptions in operations)

Why: Shulman's PCK: knowing WHERE students will struggle is more important than knowing the content itself.

column3: Superficial/procedural explanation only ('do it this way').
column4: Some conceptual explanation but relies on memorization.
column5: Explains the 'why' behind procedures; uses multiple representations.
column6: Deep conceptual teaching; connects to broader principles; encourages student reasoning.
column8:
HOTS (Understand/Analyze) + OECD (Cognitive Activation) + TEACH (Lesson Facilitation) + HOTS Observation Form (Practice #4: 'Teacher models by enacting, thinking aloud')

Why: HOTS demands teachers go beyond Remember. A teacher who only teaches procedures produces students who only memorize.

column3: Math taught purely procedurally; no use of manipulatives or visuals.
column4: Some visual aids but conceptual understanding not developed.
column5: Uses concrete → pictorial → abstract (CPA) progression; manipulatives present.
column6: CPA approach mastered; multiple solution strategies explored; math talk norms established.
column8:
FICO V3 (BM12–BM13) + EGMA Framework + Training Curriculum L0–L3 Content Expertise: Math (number sense, CPA, operations, fractions, decimals, percentages, measurement, geometry, data)

Why: CPA is gold standard for primary math. Training Curriculum builds this from L0 (basic CPA) through L3 (mentoring peers in concept-based math).

column3: Science taught from textbook only; no inquiry or observation.
column4: Some demonstration but teacher-led; students observe passively.
column5: Hands-on activities present; students make predictions and observations.
column6: Full inquiry cycle: question → predict → investigate → conclude. Students design investigations.
column8:
FICO V3 (BS12–BS13) + OECD (Cognitive Activation) + HOTS (Analyze/Evaluate/Create)

Why: Inquiry-based learning has d=0.40 effect size. Pakistani science classrooms default to lecture — this pushes toward investigation.

column3: Reading taught as decoding only; no comprehension strategies.
column4: Some reading activities but no explicit strategy instruction.
column5: Teacher models reading strategies (prediction, summarizing, questioning). Balanced approach.
column6: Balanced literacy: phonics + fluency + vocabulary + comprehension + writing integrated.
column8:
FICO V3 (BL12–BL14) + EGRA Framework + Training Curriculum L0–L3 Content Expertise: English & Urdu (phonics, phonological awareness, vocabulary, grammar, reading fluency, comprehension, writing, Arkaan Saazi, Harakaat)

Why: Balanced literacy wins. Training Curriculum builds from L0 (letter sounds, Harakaat) through L3 (coaching peers in integrated literacy).

column4: Occasional reference to other subjects but not developed.
column5: Meaningful connections made to at least one other subject area.
column6: Integrated approach; students see how math connects to science connects to language.
column8:
OECD (Cognitive Activation) + HOTS Lesson Planning ('Lesson integrates interdisciplinary or real-world applications') + Training Curriculum L2–L3 (interdisciplinary PBL lessons)

Why: Transfer is the ultimate goal of education. Pakistan's siloed curriculum desperately needs cross-curricular connections.
